land.text: the western half of Kahuripan, the share of one of Airlangga's two sons

predecessors.note: The Kediri page dates the division to 1042; the Kahuripan and Janggala pages to 1045.

land.text: the whole kingdom after the Battle of Ganter: 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari'

successors.note: 1222. Kediri is not extinguished: the Kediri page's infobox runs 'from 1042 until 1222 (1292-1293 under Jayakatwang)', and this dossier keeps the state through 1293 with no territory of its own from 1222 to 1291.

land.text: Jayakatwang's restored kingdom, ended by 'attacks by Yuan and Raden Wijaya's forces'; Majapahit's first king was enthroned on 12 November 1293

successors.note: Cliopatria draws the former Singhasari shape under Singhasari to 1293 and Majapahit from 1294.

capitals.name: Dahanapura (Daha, Kediri)
capitals.note: The page names 'Dahanapura/Daha' as the centre of the kingdom; The dot is the city of Kediri; the page gives no move.

capitals.name: Daha (Kediri), under Jayakatwang
capitals.note: The page is silent on Jayakatwang's seat; the Singhasari page calls his army 'The Kediri (Gelang-gelang) army', so the old Kediri site is assumed.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but holding from 1045, the partition year: 'In 1045, Airlangga divided Kahuripan into two kingdoms which were inherited by his two sons; Janggala and Kediri'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria begins in 1046, the Kahuripan page in 1045 (the Kediri page itself says 1042). 39,198 km2: on the grid Central Java (94 cells), Yogyakarta and the western part of East Java (44 cells), the western half of Kahuripan; the Janggala page quotes Brown, 'The western portion of Mataram became Kadiri, the eastern part Janggala'. Neither page gives an area to compare.

Same shape as 1046. Nothing on the Kediri page moves the frontier between 1046 and 1135; the page gives no infobox area. The Janggala-Panjalu war of 1049-1052 (Kahuripan page) is in the ledger as a contest without a drawn change.

correction.text: the shape unchanged but holding from 1136, when Janggala was united with Kediri: Kameswara 'married a princess of the Kingdom of Janggala, uniting the two: 1136'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the enlarged shape (73,225 km2, 286 cells) is the two 1046 halves joined, as the Janggala page's 1136 union implies; Cliopatria starts it in 1139. The Kediri page adds that 'Kediri collected spices from tributaries in southern Kalimantan and the Maluku Islands' and, from a c. 1225 Chinese source, that Java 'ruled several colonies', none dated or located, so no tint is drawn here (see notes).

correction.text: the shape unchanged but ending in 1221: 'In 1222, at the battle of Ganter, he defeated King Kertajaya of Kediri', after which 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari'

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria keeps Kediri to 1226 and starts Singhasari in 1227 with an identical 73,225 km2 shape (286 cells); the Singhasari dossier carries 1222-1226 as a new keyframe and the fief as a vassal relation. The Kediri page agrees: 'In 1222, he was forced to surrender his throne to Ken Arok'.

correction.text: Jayakatwang's restored Kediri: 'In 1292, Jayakatwang rebelled against Singhasari led by Kertanegara'; the realm is Cliopatria's 1293 Singhasari shape, which the page does not describe

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria draws 1292-1293 as Singhasari, but the Kediri infobox runs '(1292-1293 under Jayakatwang)' and the restored kingdom 'lasted only one year'. The shape (78,238 km2, 303 cells, including Madura but not Bali) is kept as the best available outline; the page gives no extent for Jayakatwang's rule.

ledger.note: 1045: Kediri (Panjalu) arises in the partition of Kahuripan. 'In 1045, Airlangga divided Kahuripan into two kingdoms which were inherited by his two sons; Janggala and Kediri.' The Kediri page dates the same division to 1042 ('In 1042, Airlangga divided his kingdom of Kahuripan into two, Janggala and Panjalu (Kadiri)') and calls Samaravijaya (1042-1051) its first king. The western half is read from Cliopatria's 1046 shape.

region.text: the frontier between Kediri (Panjalu) and Janggala; the page names no ground

ledger.note: 1049: civil war between Janggala and Panjalu after Airlangga's death. 'Airlanga died in 1049' and 'a civil war broke out between Janggala and Panjalu that continued until 1052.' The page names no ground, and the Kediri page describes no such war.

region.text: the frontier between Kediri (Panjalu) and Janggala; the page names no ground

ledger.note: 1052: the civil war with Janggala ends. 'a civil war broke out between Janggala and Panjalu that continued until 1052.' No page says who won or that a border moved.

1135: Kediri moves on Janggala under Jayabaya. 'A century later Kadiri took over the eastern Janggala empire under the command of Jayabaya in 1135-1157.' Those are Jayabaya's reign dates (the Kediri page: 'Jayabhaya (1135-1159)'), not campaign dates.
1136: the contest ends in a union of the crowns. Infobox: 'Kameswara of Kadiri married a princess of the Kingdom of Janggala, uniting the two: 1136'.

region.text: the Kingdom of Janggala, 'the northeastern part of the Kingdom of Kahuripan'

ledger.note: 1136: Kediri absorbs Janggala. 'Kameswara (1116-1136) married a princess of the Kingdom of Janggala... at which point the Kingdom of Janggala ceased to exist.' The Kediri page's infobox says only 'Janggala conquered by Jayabaya', without a year; Cliopatria draws the joined shape from 1139.

region.text: the whole Kediri kingdom of 1220, which became a fief of Singhasari

ledger.note: 1222: Kertajaya loses to Ken Arok at Ganter and Kediri becomes a fief of Singhasari. 'In 1222, at the battle of Ganter, he defeated King Kertajaya of Kediri and founded the new kingdom of Singasari.' 'Kediri became a fief under the kingdom of Singasari.' Kediri page: 'The climax of the battle between Kadiri and Tumapel occurred near the village of Ganter (Genter)' and 'In 1222, he was forced to surrender his throne to Ken Arok.' The Singhasari dossier records the fief as a vassal relation.

region.text: the realm Jayakatwang took from Singhasari; the page gives no extent, so Cliopatria's 1293 shape stands

ledger.note: 1292: Jayakatwang restores Kediri by overthrowing Singhasari. 'In 1292, Jayakatwang rebelled against Singhasari led by Kertanegara'; the infobox runs '(1292-1293 under Jayakatwang)'. The Singhasari page: 'Jayakatwang usurped and killed Kertanagara'. The extent is Cliopatria's 1293 shape; the Kediri page gives none.

region.text: the realm Jayakatwang took from Singhasari; the page gives no extent, so Cliopatria's 1293 shape stands

ledger.note: 1293: Jayakatwang's Kediri falls and Majapahit follows. The restored kingdom 'lasted only one year due to a combined attack launched by Yuan dynasty troops and Raden Wijaya troops' (Kediri Kingdom page). The Singhasari page dates the Mongol withdrawal to 31 May 1293 and Raden Vijaya's accession as Kertajasa Jayawardhana, first king of Majapahit, to 12 November 1293; no page opened dates Jayakatwang's fall to a month.

wars.name: Janggala-Panjalu civil war

zones.text: the frontier between Kediri (Panjalu) and Janggala; the page names no ground

wars.outcome: Fighting between the two halves of Kahuripan after Airlangga's death; no victor and no change of frontier given.
wars.note: Only the Kahuripan page dates it.

wars.name: Kediri's absorption of Janggala under Jayabaya
wars.outcome: Janggala is taken over by Kediri and ceases to exist with the 1136 marriage of Kameswara to a Janggala princess.
wars.note: The Janggala page's dates conflict: Kameswara 1116-1136 versus 'Kadiri took over the eastern Janggala empire under the command of Jayabaya in 1135-1157'.

wars.name: Battle of Ganter (Tumapel conquest of Kediri)

zones.text: the whole Kediri kingdom of 1220, which became a fief of Singhasari

wars.outcome: Ken Arok of Tumapel defeats Kertajaya; Kediri becomes a fief of the new kingdom of Singhasari.
wars.note: 'In 1222, at the battle of Ganter, he defeated King Kertajaya of Kediri and founded the new kingdom of Singasari.'

wars.name: Jayakatwang's revolt and the Yuan invasion of Java

zones.text: the realm Jayakatwang took from Singhasari; the page gives no extent, so Cliopatria's 1293 shape stands

wars.outcome: Jayakatwang kills Kertanagara in 1292 and rules Kediri for about a year; Mongol ships arrive near Tuban in early 1293, Raden Vijaya forces them out on 31 May 1293 and founds Majapahit.
wars.note: Singhasari page: 'The Kediri (Gelang-gelang) army attacked Singhasari simultaneously from both north and south.' The Kediri page ends the restored kingdom with 'attacks by Yuan and Raden Wijaya's forces'.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary for Kediri; the only line is the legend of a river made by Mpu Bharada's water between Kediri and Janggala. 1222-1291 the state has no territory of its own.

sources.title: Kediri Kingdom
sources.note: Identity, capital Daha, tributaries, Kertajaya, Ganter, Jayakatwang 1292-1293. No area in the infobox; its 1042 date for the founding differs from the other pages.

sources.title: Kahuripan
sources.note: The partition of 1045 and the civil war to 1052.

sources.title: Janggala
sources.note: Janggala's territory, the 1136 union, Jayabaya's conquest of Janggala.

sources.title: Singhasari
sources.note: Jayakatwang's attack of 1292, the Mongol landing of 1293, Majapahit founded 12 November 1293.

notes: Page budget up to 5: Kediri Kingdom, Kahuripan, Janggala, Ken Arok, Singhasari (the Jayabaya page was also read and added only that Jayabaya reigned 1135-1159 and 'is credited with the reunification of the Kediri Kingdom following a division'; it dates no conquest of Janggala, so it is not cited). Disagreements: the Kediri page founds the kingdom in 1042, the Kahuripan and Janggala pages date the partition to 1045; the Kediri infobox ends the first kingdom in 1222 and Cliopatria in 1226; Janggala is absorbed in 1136 (marriage) or 1135-1157 (Jayabaya), while Legge (quoted on the Janggala page) has Kediri and Janggala reunited under Ken Angrok. One state, one dossier: Jayakatwang's 1292-1293 kingdom is the restored Kediri (the infobox's own words), so it stays here; from 1222 to 1291 Kediri holds no land of its own (Singhasari's vassal fief), and Cliopatria's Singhasari shape from 1227 is Kediri's 1139 shape unchanged. Not settled: the tributary network (southern Kalimantan, the Maluku, and 'colonies' including Bali in the c. 1225 Chinese account, per the Kediri page) is undated and unlocated, so no vassal tint is drawn; a Zhu Fan Zhi page would date it. Whether Sunda or Srivijaya stood under Kediri is not on the page (it says only that Kediri 'existed alongside the Srivijaya empire'). The month of Jayakatwang's fall is on no page opened. No new gazetteer names needed.
